We travelled on a Northern Lights tour with VOYAAH in November 2025.
Initially, the group size was around 15 people; however, due to sudden cancellations, the group reduced to only 6 participants.
We are fully aware that the package price offered was calculated based on a larger group size and was extremely competitive compared to the market. Operating the tour with only six guests would have been economically unviable for most operators. However, honoring the commitment made by Sharmishtha Ma’am, VOYAAH ensured that the tour operated smoothly and without compromise—and it turned out to be a wonderful experience.
Everything promised in the itinerary was 100% delivered. In fact, because of the smaller group size, we were able to visit several additional places that were not originally part of the itinerary, which added great value to the experience.
Although there was no dedicated tour manager due to the small group size, the driver-cum-guide, Mr. Manveer, was extremely cooperative, courteous, and knowledgeable. He ensured our comfort throughout the journey and made the experience enjoyable.
The hotels provided were all 4-star properties such as Radisson Blu and Crowne Plaza, located in the city center. This allowed us to experience the local vibe and nightlife comfortably.
There were some issues during the last two days due to miscommunication between vendors; however, these were later resolved satisfactorily by the VOYAAH team.
Daily lunch or dinner arrangements were made at Indian restaurants, as per our preference, which was greatly appreciated. The vehicle provided for the tour was also in very good condition.
From the beginning, Mr. Mayank Singh, Marketing Executive (Mumbai), ensured seamless coordination for visa processing, tour-related information, and other arrangements, which made the pre-tour experience smooth and stress-free.
One area where VOYAAH can improve is communication during the tour. Having a dedicated single point of contact throughout the journey would help in addressing both minor and major concerns more efficiently, as the driver-cum-guide did not have decision-making authority and had to depend on instructions from the Bangalore/Mumbai office.
Overall, it was a very memorable and enjoyable experience. Despite operational challenges, VOYAAH stood by their commitment and delivered an excellent tour.
I would definitely recommend VOYAAH for international tours and look forward to engaging with them again for our future travels.
Thank you, VOYAAH team!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently used Thomas Cook for a vacation, and while there were some positive aspects, the overall experience left a lot to be desired, especially regarding transparency and crisis support.
**The Positives:**
* **Itinerary & Value:** The overall coverage of the itinerary was good and provided decent value for money.
* **Hotel Quality:** The hotel selections were generally of a higher standard than other tour operators like Kesari. However, consistency is an issue—in one instance, our window opened up directly to a view of a local slum.
* **Flight Assistance:** They did help us book flights for the final leg of our journey and assisted with rescheduling when those were canceled.
**The Negatives (Why I cannot recommend them):**
* **Hidden Charges & Post-Payment Demands:** This company claims to be a premium, professional travel agency, but their pricing transparency is incredibly poor. Once we negotiated and paid the full tour fee, they repeatedly came back demanding additional charges. This happened twice to us with sudden "extra" VISA and insurance fees. Furthermore, a service tip of $5 per day, per person, was hidden away in a clause that the sales team conveniently chose not to disclose upfront, costing us roughly ₹11,000 extra in dollar terms.
* **Zero Support in Jeopardy:** The true test of a premium agency is how they handle emergencies, and Thomas Cook failed completely. When our transit flight was delayed and we missed our connecting flight, they provided absolutely no help. The Sales Manager completely washed his hands of the situation, telling me I had to fight it out with the airlines locally on my own.
*Final Verdict:
Do not rely on Thomas Cook if you expect a seamless, worry-free premium service. They do not act in a decisive or supportive manner when travelers are in jeopardy. Between the hidden post-booking charges and the complete lack of accountability during transit issues, I would advise looking elsewhere.

featured_reviews.name: Ruchita Kanani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Unprofessional and Misleading Service by Thomas Cook – Bali Package

My experience with Thomas Cook has been highly unprofessional, misleading, and unacceptable. I booked a Bali tour package based on the brand’s reputation, but the service quality was far below basic customer service standards.
The booking was handled by Almaz Sayyed(Agent), along with her supervisors Dhiraj Gaikwad(AM), Sejal Ginimav, and Pritamkumar Das. From the very beginning, there was a clear lack of product knowledge and serious communication gaps. Almaz and Dhiraj were primarily focused on pushing for payment rather than providing clear and accurate information about the package.
A major issue occurred when the scanned document shared with us included an excess amount due to their mistake. When we raised this concern and requested a refund, we were conveniently informed about a so‑called company policy stating that the refund would be processed only after the completion of the tour—a policy that was never disclosed before taking payment. This reflects extremely poor transparency and unethical business practices.
Despite multiple follow‑up emails and WhatsApp messages, responses from the Thomas Cook team were extremely rare and delayed. This clearly reflects a lack of ownership and customer service mindset. The communication suggests that the team is driven only by meeting sales targets, with little to no concern for customer experience after payment is received. Such behaviour is unacceptable and reflects pathetic service standards.
It was also evident that other Thomas Cook team members did not have proper or complete knowledge of the packages they were selling. While collecting payment, we received continuous follow‑up calls, but once the package was booked, communication stopped completely. Calls were ignored, messages went unanswered, and there was zero post‑booking support.
To make matters worse, Thomas Cook added new information and requirements later, which were not disclosed during the initial discussions and were raised only after the booking was completed. This is highly misleading and unacceptable for a brand of this scale.
Another serious concern was that Almaz insisted on booking a Bali Honeymoon package, even after being clearly informed that we were not married at that time. Despite this, she proceeded with the honeymoon package, misleading us by stating that the destinations we wanted fell under that category.
The sales team creates false urgency by stating that hotels will be fully booked and good options will be lost unless payment is made immediately. However, after payment is completed, there is no follow‑up, no accountability, and the customer is forgotten.
The only positive aspect of this trip was the local Bali tour guides, who were polite, professional, and communicated clearly. Any enjoyment during the trip was solely because of them and not due to Thomas Cook’s planning or support.
I chose Thomas Cook trusting its brand name, but this decision turned out to be a mistake. Based on my experience, I strongly advise against choosing Thomas Cook. Customers would be better off selecting other tour operators who offer transparent pricing, honest communication, proper disclosure, and basic customer accountability—often at much cheaper rates.
This experience has completely eroded my trust in the Thomas Cook brand.

I would also like to convey this feedback to Mr. Mahesh Iyer, CEO of Thomas Cook. I strongly suggest hiring competent team members and ensuring they are properly trained to engage with customers professionally, transparently, and respectfully. Customers should be provided with complete and accurate information upfront, and treated with integrity—not pressured or ignored. Due to the conduct of such employees, the company’s brand reputation is being severely impacted.

featured_reviews.name: Madhura Adwankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I don’t usually write long reviews, but what Thomas Cook put us through during our Thailand trip was unbelievable.
Honestly, this has been the worst travel experience of our lives, and people deserve to know the truth before booking with them.

1. They lied about the package price

We were given a written quote of ₹42,000 + 5% TCS.
But when it came time to pay the remaining amount, they suddenly increased it to ₹49,000 and started giving excuses about USD rate — something they never mentioned earlier.
We had emails as proof, still they kept arguing.
Even after finally accepting their mistake, they forced us to pay ₹400 extra per person.
Pure cheating.

2. Staff was rude, arrogant and absolutely unprofessional

The finance person handling our case behaved like she was doing us a favour.
She never accepted their mistake, spoke rudely, and made the entire process extremely stressful.
We had to literally beg for someone else to handle our case.

3. Zero communication before the trip

One week before travelling, we had no updates, no instructions, nothing.
Every phone number in their email signatures was switched off or unreachable.
Their only answer: “Drop an email.”
How are we supposed to rely on email in another country without network?
It felt like they didn’t care at all.

4. No airport pickup in Thailand

Imagine landing in a foreign country and nobody arrives to pick you up.
All “emergency numbers” were dead.
We kept calling and calling — nothing.
Finally, after finding WiFi and sending multiple emails, someone bothered to call us.
The stress we went through at that moment is something I will never forget.

5. Cheap local truck instead of proper transport

We were promised Thomas Cook coaches.
Instead, they sent a local open truck for the 4-Island tour.
Our parents have knee problems and literally struggled to climb into that vehicle.
We even sent them videos, but nothing changed.
This is how irresponsible they are toward senior citizens.

6. Hidden mandatory fees that were never disclosed

This was the biggest shock.
Their itinerary mentioned “National Park Fees excluded” but they never told us that it was mandatory.
When we asked repeatedly whether we would be allowed to do the included activities without paying the fee, they avoided the question every single time.

At the islands, we were suddenly forced to pay at 3 places:
•	200 THB per person for 4 Islands
•	650 THB per person for Emerald pool
•	400 THB per person for Phi Phi

For 6 people, this was a huge unplanned expense.
If we knew this earlier, we would have budgeted differently — or maybe not booked with them at all.

We spent 3 days of our trip just calling, arguing, and escalating issues.
Our vacation was literally ruined.

In the end, after all the drama, they finally admitted their mistake and agreed to refund whole of the National Park Fee.
If they were right, why would they refund us?
This clearly shows they hid information from us.

In summary-
Thomas Cook completely ruined our trip with:
•	Wrong promises
•	Misleading information
•	Hidden charges
•	Rude staff
•	Zero support
•	Poor planning
•	No emergency help
•	And absolutely no accountability

This was supposed to be a relaxing family trip.
Instead, it became a trip full of stress, anger, and disappointment.

I will never book with Thomas Cook again, and I strongly warn others to think twice before trusting them.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Good management and affordable packages make them a good choice for group tours. My mother frequently travels with them and has had memorable experiences, especially on Kerala and Kashmir group trips. The trip coordinators add a personal touch and keep travelers motivated, even during challenging journeys like the Kashmir trail. Overall, I would rate their group tours 4 out of 5.

However, I would not recommend them for personal trips such as honeymoons or family travel. My recent Kerala trip was outsourced to a third-party operator, which led to poor coordination, unhelpful driving services, substandard hotels, and an unpleasant houseboat experience. The worst stay was in Munnar, where basic infrastructure issues caused serious discomfort and affected my young child’s health causing him Acute Bronchitis. Despite these issues, there was no follow-up or apology from the company. As a long-time customer, this lack of accountability broke the trust I once had in them.
